newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends up in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends up in quiet trade.

text.p: Malaysia's rubber market closed higher but volumes were negligible, with both sellers and buyers unable to agree on trading prices, dealers said on Wednesday.
They said the market was void of leads and the only excitement was news of Iran checking for SMR20 rates.
"They (Iran) are said to be looking at about one to two thousand tonnes of SMR20 for August," said a dealer.
"We have no idea what price they are seeking -- they ask for quotes and never give indications," she added.
Sellers were also cautious of quoting lower prices due to a further weakening of the ringgit on Wednesday, said traders.
At 0900 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.6360 against the US dollar in Kuala Lumpur, after opening at 2.6215 at 0200 GMT.

At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board (MRELB) quoted the benchmark RSS1 buyer for August at 241.50 cents (92 U.S. cents) a kg, up two cents from Tuesday. The SMR20 buyer for August was 1.50 cents higher at 241.50.
Traders quoted the SMR 20 at 242 cents, SMR CV at 295, SMR L at 275, SMR5 at 251, SMR10 at 243 and drum latex at 193.
The INRO's five-day average price strengthened at 186.87 Malaysian/Singapore cents a kg on July 22, compared to 186.49 on July 17. The daily indicator rose to 187.45 from 188.30 previously.
